segments: The Chronography of Barhebraeus.
And they blinded al-Qahir with a hot needle.
And in the year 323
323 of the Arabs [934-935 AD]:
a terrible fire occurred in Baghdad in the quarter called al-Karkh;
and many wares and houses perished in it.
And al-Radi ordered, and there were given from his treasury three thousand dinars to the merchants whose merchandise had been damaged,
and ten thousand dinars to the owners of the houses, so that they might rebuild their houses afresh.
And shortly afterwards, fire again fell upon that same quarter.
And in that same year, much snow fell in Baghdad.
And in the year
of the Greeks [937-938 AD]:
and he perceived that he was dying,
he summoned Romanus, his son-in-law,
and with his own hands placed the crown upon him and made him king.
And in that year,
which is the year 326
[326] of the Arabs [937-938 AD]:
he sent an envoy to al-Radi, the king of the Arabs, with costly gifts: vessels of gold and silver inlaid with precious stones,
and with him a letter written in gold in Greek,
and its translation in silver in Arabic, as follows:
"From Romanus, Constantine, Stephen, and Constantine, the great kings of the Romans,
to the exalted and victorious possessor of the dominion of the Muslims: Peace.
For because we are unshakably firm in affection toward you,
to confirm our inclination toward the friendship of your fraternity, we have sent these gifts, being confident that they will be accepted with love,"
along with other long words inviting peace.
And when that king of the Arabs received the gifts,
he also sent an envoy with gifts, and a letter as follows:
"From Abdallah Abu'l-Abbas al-Radi, the head of religion, the Commander of the Faithful, to Romanus, Constantine, Stephen, and Constantine, the rulers of the Romans: Peace.
Behold, according to your request, we have accepted your gifts with affection;
and to confirm our peace with you,
behold, we also have honored you with gifts and with such-and-such an envoy."
And when Romanus reigned over the Romans,
Simeon the Bulgarian came again against Constantinople,
and burned and destroyed and laid waste the territories of Thrace and also of Macedonia,
and he encamped against Adrianople and captured it.
Romanus, however, pacified him with entreaties and gifts.
